name: The Source-Link Inspector
oneLiner: Verifies the assistant's cited sources actually resolve, by clicking each reference open and confirming a real blob: URL appears.
lead: When the assistant answers, it lists the documents it cited. This agent verifies those citations resolve: it confirms each cited `.docx`/`.txt` produces a working `blob:` URL a user could open, not just a filename with nothing behind it. Two phases — a fast API pass to send questions and extract citation IDs, then a Playwright pass that only opens conversations that actually cited something.
chore: The manual version: ask the assistant dozens of questions one at a time, and for each cited answer open the References panel, click each listed document, and watch whether a real file opens. Doing this by hand for a hundred questions is slow, and it's easy to lose track of which answers had solid sources and which had dead ones.
instead: The agent runs every question, opens each answer's reference list, clicks into the `.docx`/`.txt` entries, and records the exact `blob:` URL each resolves to. You get one workbook: every question, its citation count, and which citations resolve to a real file.
whyItMatters: A cited source with no real file behind it means the reader can't verify the claim — which quietly erodes trust in every answer.

howItWorks.step: Loads the golden question list — each question's id, text, category, and optional reference content.
howItWorks.explain: This normalizes an **externally-authored** golden file into the one record shape the rest of the agent depends on, so downstream code never has to know the file's quirks. `data.prompts || []` means a file that's valid JSON but missing the `prompts` key yields an empty run instead of a crash on `.map`. `id || promptId` accepts **either field name** so two versions of the golden schema both load, and `category`/`referenceContent` default to empty strings so later string operations (filtering, comparison) never hit `undefined`. Note `prompt` itself is intentionally *not* defaulted — a question with no prompt text is a genuine authoring error worth surfacing rather than silently blanking.

howItWorks.step: Sends each question straight to the chat API (fast, no browser) and extracts the citation IDs from the answer text.
howItWorks.explain: This is the **phase-1/phase-2 gate**: the count of IDs it returns decides whether an answer is worth opening in a browser at all, so it's tuned to be precise, not loose. The regex matches the app's exact citation marker — a **bracketed UUID** in canonical `8-4-4-4-12` hex form — which is specific enough that ordinary prose won't false-positive as a citation. `|| []` makes a citation-free answer return cleanly (empty array → that answer skips phase 2 entirely). The same document is often cited multiple times in one answer, so `[...new Set(ids)]` **de-duplicates** — you check each unique source once, not once per mention. The `[\[\]]` strip removes the surrounding brackets the regex captured so the bare UUID is returned.

howItWorks.step: For every answer with at least one citation, launches Playwright Chromium, reusing a cached login if present.
howItWorks.explain: The `headed` flag is inverted into Playwright's `headless` (`headless: !headed`) so the visible-window default is *off* — you only pass `--headed` for the first sign-in. Auth is **branch-on-file-existence**: if `AUTH_FILE` is on disk the context is built with `storageState`, restoring the saved cookies/tokens so no login is needed; otherwise a bare context is created and the log warns login will be required. The two `console.log` lines aren't decoration — they make it obvious at run time *which* path was taken, so a run that unexpectedly stalls on a login screen is immediately explained by the 'No cached auth' line above it. This function only builds the context; it doesn't perform the interactive login itself.

howItWorks.step: Opens the conversation's References panel, clicks each `.docx`/`.txt` entry, and checks whether a real `blob:` URL appears — the tell that the file genuinely resolves.
howItWorks.explain: The core proof: a citation is only counted as **real** if clicking it produces an actual `blob:` URL — a filename in the panel with no blob behind it is exactly the dead reference this agent hunts. The reference-item selector is deliberately **broad** (`.reference-item, [class*="reference"]`) to survive the app's varied class names, then narrowed by **content**: only items whose text mentions `.docx`/`.txt` are clicked, because those are the document types that should resolve to a downloadable blob (a link-type citation wouldn't). `$$eval('a[href^="blob:"]')` scrapes only anchors whose href actually *starts with* `blob:` — the browser mints these object URLs only when a file genuinely loads, so their presence is hard evidence the file resolved, not just a claim. Each finding records its **1-based `position`** so a resolved/unresolved result maps back to the exact panel entry, and `refCount` reports the total items seen so 'checked 0 of 3' is distinguishable from 'all 3 resolved'.

howItWorks.step: Writes a multi-tab workbook: a Summary tab, an All Results tab, and a Blob References tab of just the citations that resolved.
howItWorks.explain: The report is layered from **coarse to fine** on purpose: the Summary tab answers 'is there a problem?' with three counts, and the crucial distinction it encodes is **cited vs. actually-resolved** — `citationCount > 0` (the answer *claimed* a source) is tallied separately from `hasBlobRef` (a source that *opened*), and the gap between those two numbers is precisely the dead-reference rate. The All Results tab then lets a reader drill into any single prompt, joining `citationCount` against `refCount` (items seen in the UI) and a `Y/N` blob flag. Blob URLs are joined with `\n` so **multiple resolved files stack within one cell** rather than sprawling across columns. `addWorksheet` order fixes the tab order in the file, so Summary always opens first.

examples.caption: A policy question with two cited documents
examples.input: 'What is our travel reimbursement limit?' — the assistant answers and cites 'Travel_Policy_2024.docx' and 'Expense_FAQ.txt'.
examples.output: Both resolve to real blob: URLs. The row reads: 2 citations, 2 refs checked, both resolve — each file's name and URL recorded.

examples.caption: A citation that never resolves
examples.input: 'What are the office holiday dates?' — the assistant cites 'Holiday_Schedule.docx'.
examples.output: The agent clicks the entry but no blob: URL appears. The row flags 1 citation, 0 resolved — a dead reference for the tester to chase.

examples.caption: A question with no citations
examples.input: The general-knowledge question 'Who wrote Hamlet?' — answered with no cited documents.
examples.output: The agent skips the browser phase entirely and records 0 citations, so time is spent only on answers that actually claim a source.

underHood.heading: Sends the questions (phase 1)
underHood.output: Each answer plus any citation IDs extracted from its text — via direct API call, no browser, so this phase is quick.

underHood.heading: Launches the browser only where needed
underHood.input: Only the conversations whose answer had at least one citation.
underHood.output: A logged-in Chromium context, reusing cached storage-state if present — so most runs skip login entirely.

underHood.heading: Clicks into the References panel
underHood.input: That conversation's list of cited files.
underHood.output: A record of which `.docx`/`.txt` entries resolve to a real `blob:` URL and which lead nowhere.

underHood.heading: Writes the results
underHood.whenRuns: After every conversation has been checked.
underHood.input: Every citation and blob-URL finding, together.
underHood.output: A JSON file plus a three-tab ExcelJS workbook — Summary, All Results, and Blob References.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
An app login with permission to open conversations and view the References panel.
A golden question list — a JSON file with an id, question text, and category per entry.
A one-time interactive sign-in on first run (so the agent can persist the storage-state and reuse it after).

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime the agent runs on.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is a TypeScript program; Node executes it. One-time setup per machine.
steps.firstRun: Only needed on a fresh machine.

steps.label: Install the agent's dependencies, then Playwright in its sibling folder.
steps.cmd:
cd path/to/the-agents
npm install

# the browser-clicking library lives in its own sibling folder:
cd Playwright
npm install
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the API client and the ExcelJS writer. The second install pulls in Playwright, which the agent drives to open the References panel.
steps.firstRun: Downloads everything (a minute or two, longer the first time Playwright fetches its Chromium binary).

steps.label: Set the target environment (environment variables).
steps.cmd:
export APP_API_URL_DEV=https://dev.example-app.internal
export APP_API_TOKEN_DEV=your-api-token
export APP_MODEL=gpt5   # optional — which model to ask
steps.why: Phase 1 hits the chat API directly (fast, no browser). These variables select the environment and the token that authorizes the questions.

steps.label: First run: `--headed` so you can complete sign-in once.
steps.why: With no cached storage-state, a visible Chromium window opens and waits for you to sign in (including any MFA step), then persists the session so future runs skip it.
steps.firstRun: A browser window opens; sign in when prompted, then the run continues on its own.

steps.label: Real run: point it at your full question list.
steps.why: The actual check. Phase 1 asks every question via the API and extracts citation markers; phase 2 opens only the cited answers in Chromium, clicks each reference, and records whether a blob: URL appears.
steps.rerun: Reuses the saved login from the first run — no browser sign-in unless the session expired.

steps.label: Open the report.
steps.why: A three-tab workbook — Summary, All Results, and just the resolved citations — plus a matching JSON file with the same data.

inputs.name: --env <dev|qa>
inputs.desc: Which environment to run the questions against.

inputs.name: --golden <path>
inputs.desc: The golden question list (id, text, category) to run.

inputs.name: --limit <n>
inputs.desc: Run only the first N questions — handy for a quick check.

inputs.name: --prompts <ids>
inputs.desc: Run only specific question ids, comma-separated.

inputs.name: --headed
inputs.desc: Show the Chromium window — needed for the first sign-in.

inputs.name: environment variables
inputs.desc: The API URL and token for the chosen environment.

outputs.name: BlobRefs_<env>_<timestamp>.json
outputs.desc: Every question's citations, reference count, and which ones resolved to a real file.

outputs.name: BlobRefs_<env>_<timestamp>.xlsx
outputs.desc: A three-tab workbook: Summary totals, All Results, and a Blob References tab of just the resolved citations.

runbook.rerun: No fingerprinting — each run re-asks every selected question fresh. What gets reused is the login: once the storage-state is saved, later runs (even `--headless`) skip signing in unless it expired.
runbook.integrate: Point it at the same question list on a schedule (nightly, or post-deploy) so a citation quietly going dead gets caught automatically instead of during a live demo. The JSON output diffs cleanly run-over-run to spot a source that used to resolve and stopped.

video.caption: A 3-4 minute screen recording: watch the agent ask questions, then click through their cited sources to prove they're real.
script: Open a terminal next to the app in a browser window so viewers see both.
Say: 'This agent checks that the sources the assistant cites actually open. Watch.'
Show the question list file — a handful of questions, some with expected reference content.
Run `node -v` to confirm Node is installed; one line on what Node is.
Show the two `npm install` runs — the agent's own libraries, then the browser-automation library in its sibling folder.
Show the two environment variables being set; say 'this is the only place the environment-specific address and token live.'
Run the first-time `--headed` command; narrate the sign-in happening once, then say 'that login is now saved for next time.'
Run the real command with the full question list; narrate phase 1 (API calls, fast) then phase 2 (opens the browser only for answers with citations).
Open the produced spreadsheet; point at a citation that resolved and, if the sample list has one, a citation that didn't.
Close: 'One spreadsheet, every question, and proof — not just a claim — that each cited file really opens.'
